questions.text: Where was Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) born?
questions.explanation: He was born in Makkah Mukarramah in the tribe of Quraish.

questions.text: How old was Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) when his mother passed away?
questions.explanation: His mother died when he was only six years old.

questions.text: Who took care of him after his mother's death?
questions.explanation: His grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib took care of him.

questions.text: At what age did he come under the guardianship of his uncle Abu Talib?
questions.explanation: When he reached the age of eight his grandfather passed away and Abu Talib became his guardian.

questions.text: Where did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) take Hazrat Khadija's caravan of goods?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Khadija entrusted him to take her caravan of goods to Syria.

questions.text: Who accompanied him on the trade journey and reported his honesty to Hazrat Khadija?
questions.explanation: Her old and trusted slave Maysarah accompanied him and reported his integrity.

questions.text: Even his enemies called him 'Al-Amin', which means:
questions.explanation: He was called Al-Sadiq (the truthful) and Al-Amin (the trustworthy one).

questions.text: To which emperor did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) write a letter inviting him to Islam?
questions.explanation: He wrote to Heraclius, the Emperor of Byzantium.

questions.text: Who did Heraclius question about the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: Heraclius summoned Abu Sufyan, who admitted the Prophet's honesty and trustworthiness.

questions.text: In the case of the woman from Bani Makhzum, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) taught us about:
questions.explanation: He refused to excuse her crime due to her status, showing equal justice for all.

questions.text: Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of which month?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr commemorates the end of Ramadan and the start of Shawwal.

questions.text: Shawwal is which month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The lesson calls Shawwal the 10th month in the Islamic calendar.

questions.text: The night before Eid-ul-Fitr is known as:
questions.explanation: After the Eid crescent is announced, the night is known as Chand Raat.

questions.text: What is 'fitrana'?
options: Obligatory payment to the poor before Eid prayer
questions.explanation: Fitrana is an obligatory payment to the poor, given before Eid namaz.

questions.text: Money or gifts children receive from elders on Eid is called:
questions.explanation: Kids get 'Eidi' from elders as new currency notes or gifts.

questions.text: What did Usman forget to bring for the kheer?
questions.explanation: Mother said he forgot milk and rice, the main ingredients of kheer.

questions.text: Who wrote 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'?
questions.explanation: The poem is by William Butler Yeats.

questions.text: What does the poet want to build at Innisfree?
options: A small cabin of clay and wattles
questions.explanation: 'And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made.'

questions.text: How many bean-rows will the poet have at Innisfree?
questions.explanation: 'Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee.'

questions.text: What does the poet hear 'in the deep heart's core'?
options: Lake water lapping on the shore
questions.explanation: He hears lake water lapping with low sounds by the shore, in the deep heart's core.

questions.text: Where is the poet standing when he thinks of Innisfree?
options: On the roadway or on the pavements grey
questions.explanation: 'While I stand on the roadway, or on the pavements grey.'

questions.text: The poet wants to go to Innisfree because he longs for:
options: a peaceful life close to nature
questions.explanation: The poem contrasts the grey city with peaceful natural life at Innisfree.

questions.text: Major Shabbir Sharif was awarded the:
questions.explanation: He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider, the highest military award.

questions.text: When was Major Shabbir Sharif born?
questions.explanation: He was born on April 28, 1943, in Kunjah, Gujrat.

questions.text: Major Shabbir Sharif was the nephew of which Nishan-e-Haider holder?
questions.explanation: He was the nephew of Nishan-e-Haider holder Major Raja Aziz Bhatti.

questions.text: Which award did he receive on completing training at Pakistan Military Academy, Kakul?
questions.explanation: He completed his training and was awarded the Sword of Honour.

questions.text: In which war did Major Shabbir Sharif embrace martyrdom?
questions.explanation: He fought in the 1971 Indo-Pakistani War in the Sulemanki Sector.

questions.text: How old was Major Shabbir Sharif at the time of martyrdom?
questions.explanation: At the time of martyrdom he was just 28 years old.

questions.text: Major Shabbir Sharif is the only soldier to receive both the Nishan-e-Haider and the:
questions.explanation: He is the only one to have received both Nishan-e-Haider and Sitara-e-Jurat.

questions.text: Who moved in next door to Haziq and Ahmad?
questions.explanation: They saw a family moving next door and welcomed them with dessert.

questions.text: What did the mother first send to the new neighbours?
questions.explanation: Mother gave them a bowl of dessert to take to the new neighbours.

questions.text: What was the name of the boy who sat at the window?
questions.explanation: His mother told them the boy's name was Jasim.

questions.text: Why could Jasim not walk?
options: He had polio as a child
questions.explanation: Jasim had polio at the age of two; his legs remained dysfunctional.

questions.text: Why was Jasim afraid of school?
options: He was bullied by naughty boys in his previous school
questions.explanation: He had a phobia of school because he had been bullied by naughty boys.

questions.text: At first, what did Haziq and Ahmad think of Jasim?
questions.explanation: Since he shut the window on seeing them, they thought him proud and rude.

questions.text: The lesson in Unit 5 teaches us to:
options: treat special people with kindness and friendship
questions.explanation: It teaches harmony: we should understand and befriend people with disabilities.

questions.text: Why did Tina and her mother go shopping?
options: For a big party that night
questions.explanation: They had a big party that night and needed things to cook a grand dinner.

questions.text: What did Tina find on the way back from the market?
options: A woman collapsed on the road
questions.explanation: They found a woman lying collapsed on the road.

questions.text: What does CPR stand for?
questions.explanation: Tina continued cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) until the ambulance came.

questions.text: How many uninterrupted chest compressions did Tina give?
questions.explanation: She provided 30 uninterrupted chest compressions.

questions.text: Why did Tina ask the crowd to move back?
options: So the lady could get fresh air
To clear the road for cars
questions.explanation: She asked the crowd to move back so the lady could get fresh air.

questions.text: What was Tina studying?
questions.explanation: Tina is a medical student.

questions.text: According to the doctor, how many people know what to do in an emergency?
questions.explanation: Only one in 20 people know what to do in an emergency.

questions.text: CPR helps by providing oxygen-rich blood flow to the:
questions.explanation: CPR keeps oxygen-rich blood flowing to the brain and other organs until treatment.

questions.text: What kind of person was Mr. Shan, the newly appointed minister?
questions.explanation: Mr. Shan was rude, offensive and a corrupt minister who never worked without bribery.

questions.text: Why did the poor farmer come to Mr. Shan?
options: For approval of a water pump in his area
questions.explanation: The farmer came for the approval of a water pump in his area.

questions.text: What did Mr. Shan do when the farmer could not pay a bribe?
options: Tore up his application and had him thrown out
questions.explanation: He rudely tore up the application and ordered his guards to throw the farmer out.

questions.text: According to the Hadith quoted in the lesson, the curse of Allah is on:
options: both the briber and the recipient
questions.explanation: 'May the curse of Allah be on the briber and the recipient.'

questions.text: Why did nobody stand up against Mr. Shan?
options: He had a strong wealthy background
questions.explanation: Due to his strong wealthy background, nobody stood up against him.

questions.text: Where were Danish and his grandfather lying on the hot summer night?
options: On the roof of their home
questions.explanation: Danish was lying with his grandfather on the roof of their home.

questions.text: According to Grandfather, why did they not need air conditioners in the past?
options: Many trees and green plots kept the temperature low
questions.explanation: Many trees and green plots kept the temperature low.

questions.text: What does 'overpopulation' mean, as explained in the lesson?
options: Too few people in a country
So large a population that people suffer as a result
questions.explanation: Overpopulation is a situation where population is so large that people suffer as a result.

questions.text: Why did people migrate from villages to cities, according to the lesson?
options: To get more opportunities and meet basic needs
questions.explanation: People migrated to cities to get more and meet their basic needs.

questions.text: The excessive use of coal, oil and fossil fuels is:
options: creating a negative impact on our planet
questions.explanation: Excessive use of fossil fuels is creating a negative impact on the planet.

questions.text: Why was the river near Grandfather's home no longer good for swimming?
options: It was polluted by human waste
questions.explanation: They loved to swim in it, but it was now polluted by human waste.

questions.text: Who was Mr. Akbar in the lesson?
options: A newly appointed teacher in the town
questions.explanation: Mr. Akbar was a newly appointed teacher in the town.

questions.text: Where did Mr. Akbar see Ameena reading?
questions.explanation: He saw little Ameena sitting under the light pole reading an old book.

questions.text: What was the hardest challenge Ameena faced in getting education?
questions.explanation: One of the hardest challenges she encountered was poverty.

questions.text: What did Ameena's father do for a living?
questions.explanation: Her father was a scrap picker and could not bear her school expenses.

questions.text: Where did Ameena get books to read?
questions.explanation: She used to find old books from the scrap her father brought home.

questions.text: What did Mr. Akbar promise the villagers?
options: Free teaching with books and stationery
questions.explanation: He promised to teach without any fee, with books and stationery from school.

questions.text: How did Ameena help the landlord?
options: She gave first aid for a snake bite
questions.explanation: She tied his leg near the wound, washed it with soap and water and covered it with a clean dressing.

questions.text: What did Ameena want to become?
questions.explanation: She told the doctor she wanted to be a doctor.

questions.text: Modern communication devices have made the world a:
questions.explanation: Computers, mobile phones and electronic media have made the world a global village.

questions.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, what became a life saviour for many people?
questions.explanation: Technology became a life saviour; people worked and studied from home.

questions.text: How has technology helped in education, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: Students are facilitated with smart classes, multimedia, e-libraries and e-books.

questions.text: Which are medical devices mentioned in the lesson?
questions.explanation: X-rays, scan machines, operation devices and pacemakers help doctors and patients.

questions.text: On which planet have scientists 'marked their presence'?
questions.explanation: The lesson says they have marked their presence on Mars.

questions.text: Which day is the poem in Unit 11 about?
questions.explanation: The poem begins: 'Who knew that the day of 14th of August will tell the world...'

questions.text: Who wrote the poem about 14th August in Unit 11?
questions.explanation: The poem is by Dr. Tafazzal.

questions.text: In the poem, Pakistan is called a home for a:
questions.explanation: 'A lovely land with sacred lands, and a home for a Musalman.'

questions.text: 'A Quaid's effort, a poet's dream' refers to:
questions.explanation: Pakistan was the effort of Quaid-e-Azam and the dream of the poet Allama Iqbal.

questions.text: Who is the founder of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is the founder of Pakistan.

questions.text: Why did Ms. Sara ask Basit to do his assignment again?
options: He could not complete it on time
questions.explanation: Basit could not complete it; Zubair advised him to complete tasks on time.

questions.text: What did Shiza and Tania learn about in their lesson?
questions.explanation: That day they had a lesson about good citizenship.

questions.text: What did Shiza and Tania do to improve their area?
options: Cleaned the street and planted trees
questions.explanation: They cleaned their street and garden and planted new trees.

questions.text: How long did it take the children to give their area a new look?
questions.explanation: Within two hours a new look of their area emerged.

questions.text: What did Shiza do when she saw strangers enter her neighbour's house?
options: Called the helpline and warned her neighbours
questions.explanation: She called the helpline and told the neighbours to lock their inner door.

questions.text: How did the strangers get into the house?
options: One climbed the wall and opened the gate
questions.explanation: One of them climbed the wall and opened the gate for his friends.

questions.text: A good citizen must:
options: keep surroundings clean and be vigilant
questions.explanation: The teacher said a citizen must care for neighbours, keep surroundings clean and stay vigilant.
